title: Five years: the ways
hookLine: ragas, teachings, the code, the streams, the thought
tomorrow: a dorm, a roommate, no Bebe. which prayers make the cut?

lines: A RAGA, A RULE OR A LINE?
cards: A raga, a rule or a line? Simran's speech needs one sentence about what changed her, and she can't pick. Then she notices something odd about the book she's been reading from all year.
A music app sorts songs by artist. Plenty of books go by who wrote them, or when. The Guru Granth Sahib is sorted mostly by raga, by musical mode.
And inside those sections, after the Gurus' hymns, come voices that weren't Sikh Gurus at all.

teach.h: THE BHAGATS: KABIR, FARID, NAMDEV, RAVIDAS.
teach.b: Those voices are the bhagats, saints whose hymns the Gurus gathered into the Granth. Kabir, who calls himself a weaver. Sheikh Farid, a Sufi Muslim.
Namdev and Ravidas, and others. So the puzzle: why would a Sikh scripture keep the songs of people who were never Sikhs? Kabir answers it himself, in a hymn on Ang 1349, paraphrased.
First God made the light, and Kabir uses the name Allah here. Everyone is the work of the same Maker.

teach.h: FROM ONE LIGHT, THE WHOLE WORLD.
teach.b: From one light the whole world came. So who is good, and who is bad? The Granth's test wasn't the label on the singer.
It was the song: the One, the Name, people seen as equal. That's the ways, folded together. The ragas carry it as music.
The teaching, Gurmat, is the Guru's way of seeing.
The code, the Rehat Maryada, gives it a shape for daily life. The streams are Sikh groups who keep different emphases and still bow to the same Granth.
And the thought runs underneath all of it: one light. Simran has her sentence. Not a rule, not a raga.
A line, sung in a raga, by a weaver.

how: In the gurdwara the hymns of the bhagats, Kabir, Sheikh Farid, Namdev, Ravidas and others, are read and sung as Gurbani alongside the Gurus' own hymns, each in its raga.

s: the Guru Granth Sahib holds only the Sikh Gurus' words
it also holds the bhagats: Kabir, Sheikh Farid, Namdev, Ravidas and others.
most of the Granth is sorted by raga
its main sections follow musical modes, not authors or dates.
Kabir's hymn on Ang 1349 says the whole world came from one light
so, he asks, who is good and who is bad?

games.q: your youth group picks a reading for an interfaith evening. someone says only a Guru's own hymn is really Sikh scripture. what fits?
o: a bhagat's hymn in the Granth is Gurbani too; Kabir's one light fits the night.
only the Gurus' own hymns count; the bhagats are a respectful extra.
pick any Kabir poem from any book; it's all the same thing anyway.
games.why: the bhagats' hymns sit inside the Granth's ragas and are sung as Gurbani. the Granth kept them for the song, not the singer's label.

practice: Count on your fingers the things that changed you over these years: a line, a person, a habit, a meal, a song. Stop when the count feels true, and stay with the last one you counted, thanking it.
